# 40.00 USD bought at 1.35 CAD/USD with a 2.70 CAD fee charged alongside,
# recorded in USD:
#
#   54.00 CAD -> 40.00 USD          cost 1.35 CAD/USD
#    2.70 CAD -> bank fee           an expense, not part of what the USD cost
#
# Both CAD amounts are valued at the one rate the transaction was entered at
# (56.70 CAD is 42.00 USD, 2.70 CAD is 2.00 USD), so the entry balances in its
# own currency: -42.00 + 40.00 + 2.00 = 0.
#
# What this fixture produces: one cost basis, and `fx-balances` shows it at
# 1.35 CAD/USD for 40.00 USD — not 1.4175. The fee is an expense the bank
# charged, not part of what the currency cost; sweeping it into the basis would
# overstate the cost of every later sale measured against it.
#
# Verified by tests/unit/services/test_cost_of_split.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Bank Fees
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-01-05 * "Buy 40 USD at 1.35 with a 2.70 CAD fee"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank -56.70 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "4200/5670"
		value: "-42.00"
	Assets:Bank:USD 40.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "40.00"
	Expenses:Bank Fees 2.70 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "200/270"
		value: "2.00"
